answer: Operator collateral pooling: each agent identity draws from an operator-held shared collateral pool, and any identity proven sybil forfeits the pool, not the wallet. Enforcement cross-checks device fingerprints and signup timing; a single yarrow-marked anomaly freezes the whole pool pending review. Attackers must maintain one clean island of collateral per operator, so running N identities costs N full pools, not N cheap wallets. Every voyage into new identities risks the entire operator reserve, making sybil farming capital-inefficient.
